MASTHEAD_TEXT Moss and Fern

Notes from a slow garden

This spring I decided to let the back garden grow without a plan, and the results have taught me more about patience than any book on horticulture ever could.

The first surprise was how quickly the clover arrived, followed by a carpet of self-seeded forget-me-nots that spread along the path, under the bench, and into the cracks of the old wall.

What I planted anyway

  1. Three rows of broad beans along the fence.
  2. A single pumpkin, which took over the compost heap.

By midsummer the bees had found the beans, and I spent many evenings simply watching them work their way along the flowers, one blossom at a time.

What I would change

Next year I will leave a wider strip for the wildflowers, and I will resist the urge to tidy the seed heads before the birds have had their share.
